high.title: Ringgit closes lower ahead of key US economic data
high.summary: The ringgit depreciated to 4.0825/4.0870 against the US dollar at close, retreating from an intraday high of RM4.04. The US Dollar Index rose 0.23% to 101.338, supporting the greenback. Key US data releases including JOLTS and Conference Board Consumer Confidence are expected to influence near-term ringgit direction.

high.title: Bursa ends on a softer note
high.summary: The FBM KLCI eased 1.85 points to close at 1,664.06, weighed down by persistent foreign selling and external uncertainties despite stronger regional performance. Analysts note that the pullback has made selected blue-chip valuations more attractive, potentially encouraging bargain hunting. Near-term volatility is expected to persist, with domestic institutional buying seen as a key support factor.

high.title: Ringgit strengthens against major regional currencies
high.summary: The ringgit appreciated to 4.0680/4.0735 against the USD from 4.0860/4.0910 at Friday's close, strengthening across major currencies. Lower crude oil prices amid US-Iran peace negotiations supported the ringgit's gains. Key US economic data releases this week, including nonfarm payrolls and ISM indices, will be critical in determining further USD direction.

high.title: Bursa pares earlier losses to end slightly lower
high.summary: The FBM KLCI closed slightly lower but recovered from earlier losses as bargain hunting emerged in the afternoon session. FBM 70 and FBM Small Cap indices closed higher, indicating selective accumulation in mid- and small-cap stocks. Market sentiment remained cautious due to geopolitical risks from the US-Iran ceasefire fragility and China's tightened export controls on Japanese companies.

high.title: Ringgit extends gains against US dollar, regional peers
high.summary: The ringgit extended gains as US economic data showed underlying weakness, with consumer spending rising only 0.5% in Q1 2026 despite headline GDP beating expectations at 2.1%. Trimmed Fed rate hike expectations pulled US yields lower, relieving pressure on Asian currencies including the ringgit. PCE inflation at 4.1% came in line with forecasts, providing further currency stability signals.

high.title: Ringgit opens lower as strong US GDP lifts dollar
high.summary: The ringgit opened weaker at 4.1170/4.1270 against the US dollar as better-than-expected US Q1 GDP of 2.1% initially boosted the greenback. However, the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz improved risk appetite and limited the ringgit's decline. The US Dollar Index fell 0.18% after PCE data release, with analysts questioning the sustainability of the dollar rally amid weak consumer spending trends.

high.title: Selling pressure drags Bursa lower
high.summary: The FBM KLCI dropped 1.09% or 18.31 points to close at 1,663.82, driven by broad-based weakness in industrial and banking heavyweights. Banking stocks faced sustained pressure as investors priced in a prolonged higher-for-longer global interest rate environment following hawkish signals from the ECB, Bank of Japan, and US Fed. Sentiment remained cautious ahead of the US PCE inflation data release, a key indicator that could influence the Fed's future monetary policy trajectory.

high.title: Ringgit continues stellar performance, ends higher for third consecutive day
high.summary: The ringgit appreciated to 4.1160/4.1200 against the US dollar, marking a third consecutive day of gains and strengthening against a basket of major currencies. The positive momentum is supported by declining crude oil prices, with Brent crude at US$72.86 per barrel — down 38.3% from its recent high — which could ease US inflation and potentially alter the Fed's rate hike path. Upcoming US PCE inflation data is identified as a near-term key focus that may further influence ringgit direction.

medium.title: US House Committee investigates Merck, AbbVie China drug trials
medium.summary: US lawmakers are investigating major pharmaceutical companies including Merck, AbbVie, Pfizer, Eli Lilly, and Bristol-Myers Squibb over their clinical trial operations in China, particularly in Xinjiang and military hospitals. The scrutiny raises geopolitical and compliance risks for these global pharma giants. This could affect pharmaceutical sector sentiment and supply chain considerations relevant to Malaysian healthcare and pharma investors.

medium.title: Bursa gains in early trade on improved risk sentiment
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI edged up 0.24 points to 1,666.15 in early trade, with positive market breadth showing gainers outnumbering losers. However, analysts cautioned that ongoing Middle East tensions and external uncertainties were likely to keep trading range-bound between 1,660 and 1,670. Low trading volumes reflected continued investor caution.

medium.title: Ringgit gains in early trade on weaker US Dollar Index
medium.summary: The ringgit opened stronger at 4.0605/4.0730 against the US dollar as the DXY declined 0.25% to 101.10 points. Analysts expected the ringgit to trade within a 4.06 to 4.08 range pending key US data releases. Upcoming JOLTS and Consumer Confidence data were highlighted as potential market-moving catalysts for the currency.

medium.title: Stocks adrift, oil up as US-Iran halt renewed attacks
medium.summary: Global markets showed limited direction as US-Iran tensions resurfaced following tit-for-tat strikes after an Iranian projectile hit a cargo vessel in the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude rose 0.85% to US$72.6 per barrel and WTI gained over 1%, with geopolitical uncertainty driving oil price volatility. Asian markets were broadly lower, with South Korea's KOSPI down nearly 2% and Japan's Nikkei slipping 1%, reflecting cautious global sentiment relevant to Malaysian market performance.

medium.title: Bursa retreats at open as sentiment turns cautious
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI fell 5.70 points to 1,662.04 at the open as Wall Street's decline in technology stocks and renewed US-Iran geopolitical tensions dampened sentiment. Analysts noted current levels present buying opportunities but advised caution, with the index expected to hover between 1,665 and 1,675. The weakness in AI-related counters globally continues to weigh on market undertone.

medium.title: Ringgit slightly higher against greenback, supported by low oil prices
medium.summary: At the opening, the ringgit was pegged at 4.0855/4.0950 against the USD, supported by lower crude oil prices and continued US-Iran negotiations. Continued shipping through the Straits of Hormuz suggested potential resolution of oil supply concerns. Analysts expected the USD/MYR pair to trade within the RM4.08 to RM4.10 range for the day.

medium.title: Six-month extension for stamp duty disclosure programme
medium.summary: LHDN extended the voluntary disclosure programme for stamp duty, covering instruments executed between Jan 1, 2023 and Dec 31, 2025, with penalties automatically waived upon payment. Applications and payments must be completed by Dec 31 this year, and compliant instruments will not be subject to audit. This is relevant for Malaysian businesses and property transactions that may have outstanding stamp duty obligations.

medium.title: Banking stocks lift Bursa at close
medium.summary: The FBM KLCI closed up 0.24% at 1,667.75, supported by a late rebound in banking stocks and continued positive momentum in the telecommunications sector. Market sentiment remained cautious amid global volatility surrounding AI investment themes. The index recovered from intraday losses to finish marginally higher, signalling resilience despite uncertain global conditions.

medium.title: Bursa opens slightly higher on bargain hunting
medium.summary: Bursa Malaysia opened slightly higher with the FBM KLCI rising 1.82 points to 1,665.64, driven by bargain hunting despite mixed Wall Street performance. Market breadth was negative with decliners outpacing gainers 220 to 125, reflecting cautious investor sentiment. Volatility in AI-related stocks and Apple's price hikes weighed on overall market mood.
